markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize **GRU4Rec with a gated recent-window representation**, trained under a fixed BPR-max configuration. Retain this feasible hypothesis; text enrichment and dropout consistency remain alternatives. No new experimental results are claimed.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Recency weighting changes supervision, whereas window pooling changes inference context; their effects require separate comparisons. (2) The previous latest-item residual exposes immediate history but risks learning frequent transitions. A four-item mean adds evidence while discarding its internal order. (3) Electronics’ 22.31% small-margin and 9.01% wrong-rank rates motivate discrimination experiments, but training margins do not establish validation gains.

**Insights from related work.** (1) [STAMP](https://github.com/uestcnlp/STAMP/blob/master/model/STAMP_rsc.py) combines latest-item and session representations; its mean covers the whole session, providing precedent rather than evidence for recent-window averaging. (2) [NARM](https://arxiv.org/abs/1711.04725) combines final GRU state and attended recurrent states. Its component results support testing hybrid context, without establishing parameter-matched superiority here. (3) [BPR-max](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf) emphasizes high-scoring negatives through a differentiable weighted sigmoid sum. Its sampler, activation and reduction must be distinguished from the host baseline.

The framework separates three directions:

| Direction | Intervention | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Supervision | Fixed BPR-max; optional target-age weighting | Current context remains implicit |
| Context | Gated recent-window representation | Averaging loses order and may dilute specific intent |
| Item specificity | Joint title/description encoder | Semantic similarity can favor substitutes |

Three candidate ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment lists a positive and a limitation in that order.

| Idea | Scores | Assessment by criterion |
|---|---|---|
| Recent-window gate | 3/6/7/6/4 | Originality: focused extension / established pooling and gating. Potential: tests context length / incremental contribution. User: targets stale interests and broad affinity / cannot establish compatibility. Model: tests ambiguous rankings / larger margins may reflect scale. Difficulty: small module / controlled integration and export require care. |
| Joint title/description pooling | 4/6/6/6/6 | Originality: constrained adaptation / established text fusion. Potential: sparse-item sharing / metadata dependence. User: finer specificity / substitutes may rise. Model: shared item evidence / discrimination gains unproven. Difficulty: simple pooling / preprocessing and scoring changes. |
| Dropout consistency auxiliary loss | 3/5/4/6/5 | Originality: compatible adaptation / established consistency learning. Potential: stable features / augmentation may explain gains. User: robust context / indirect intent alignment. Model: regularizes ambiguity / false negatives remain. Difficulty: shared encoder / extra passes and controls. |

**Selected algorithm.** Blend corrected GRU features with a projected causal mean of the last four real input embeddings using a scalar gate. This explicitly targets stale interests outranking recent preferences and broad historical affinity displacing specific recent matches. Fixed BPR-max addresses weak sampled separation. Compatibility, complementary value and immediate intent remain unverified.

First compare ungated versus gated models under identical training settings. If affordable, compare windows one and four using identical gates/projections; broader controls test full-history pooling and ordering. Track common sampled margins, norms and earlier-history sensitivity, alongside simulator judgments about immediate choice, stale interests and duplication. Select only by pinned macro validation HR@10. Retain one jointly trained GRU checkpoint per category and matching predictor export.

idea.description: Extend the supplied corrected GRU4Rec with a scalar-gated causal mean of the four most recent real input embeddings. Train this internal path jointly with the GRU under a declared, fixed BPR-max configuration. Each category retains exactly one independently trained network and one selected checkpoint. Use vectorized pooling as a candidate implementation, subject to numerical and runtime verification.
idea.motivation: The recent-window path explicitly targets two observed user failures: older interests outranking recent preferences, and broad historical affinity displacing more specific recent matches. Several recent observations may provide stronger evidence than one, but their mean loses internal order and can dilute the latest preference. BPR-max addresses weak sampled discrimination, especially Electronics’ measured 22.31% small-margin and 9.01% negative-over-positive rates. These are training diagnostics, not validation results. Neither pooling nor BPR-max establishes ownership satisfaction, compatibility, complementary benefit, current intent or unobserved simulator traits.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integration scope: the corrected host baseline source is absent from the prompt. This is an integration component, not a reproducible replacement train.py or an executed experiment. Preserve the supplied GRU backbone, padding-invariant recurrent updates, input transformations, scoring activation, sampler, reducer, optimizer and empty-history behavior unless a change is explicitly declared as a separate intervention. Attach the module after the baseline feature transformation, in its scoring dimension. Pool the exact transformed input embeddings already supplied to the GRU, including the same dropout realization; do not introduce another embedding lookup or dropout draw. Only current and earlier observed inputs enter the pool, never shifted positive targets.

Architecture: use window=4 as a prespecified initial hypothesis. The gate receives the GRU feature and pooled embedding, has zero initial weights and bias -4, and therefore starts near 1.8%. Initialize the projection with the documented baseline policy. This makes the initial architecture close to, but not exactly, the baseline. Initialize added parameters separately so shared tensors retain identical initial values across comparisons. A scalar gate is not an explanation of intent. Mean pooling discards order within its window; the retained GRU remains order sensitive. Padding outputs must be zero, and the final readout uses the maximum nonpadding index, never count-1.

Vectorized pooling: cumulative valid-item counts identify each position’s last K real inputs. Zero-prefixed embedding sums and searchsorted boundaries compute their causal mean without a B x L x K x D intermediate. Explicitly zero padded embeddings before accumulation and mask padded outputs. The implementation handles internal gaps, all-padding rows, K=1, K>L and empty sequences. Floating-point work/storage is O(BLD); integer boundary lookup adds search overhead. Vectorization does not establish a speed improvement. Accumulate reduced-precision embeddings in FP32; subtraction of large prefixes can still suffer cancellation, including small erroneous dependence on embeddings outside the intended window. Compare output and gradient errors against a queue reference at actual sequence lengths. If errors are unacceptable, retain the reference or a verified alternative rather than assuming numerical equivalence.

Objective: implement paper Eq. (16), -log(sum_j softmax(n)_j * sigmoid(p-n_j) + epsilon) + lambda * sum_j softmax(n)_j * n_j^2. This is not the softmax-weighted average of negative log-sigmoids. Keep softmax weights differentiable and normalize across the complete negative pool, including when scores are chunked. There is no additional division by negative count. The score penalty lambda is distinct from optimizer weight decay. Preserve the host score activation and epsilon convention in controlled comparisons. Official implementations use epsilon=1e-24; choosing zero is a declared deviation, even if numerically negligible in ordinary ranges. Establish a named score_reg=0 control unless the host already specifies a different setting; do not silently transfer official bpreg=1.0. Changing lambda or activation alongside the readout confounds attribution. Monitor score norms, means and extrema because scaling affects margins and negative concentration. Common shifts leave the unregularized loss invariant at its score inputs; the squared-score penalty breaks this invariance.

Sampling and reduction: record the actual host negative-ID construction, exclusions, duplicate policy and reduction before execution. If the baseline supplies one negative, expanding to K=32 total negative columns is a separate objective/pool intervention rather than an effect of pooling. K=1 with lambda=0 provides a pairwise-BPR equality check but cannot test hard-negative emphasis. Official PyTorch GRU4Rec combines minibatch targets with shared replacement draws proportional to training frequency^sample_alpha; it excludes each row’s diagonal target column only. Duplicate negatives and other copies of that positive remain. Its ELU output transformation, configured-batch-size denominator and session batching must not be silently substituted for the host’s sequential B x L training. Official behavior is a reference, not a requirement to change the corrected baseline. No logQ correction is proposed for BPR-max. Gather valid positions before expensive negative scoring, preserve the original position/window/user reduction and skip empty valid batches.

Affordable comparison order: retain the supplied baseline reference, establish an unweighted BPR-max control if necessary, and compare ungated versus window=4 gated GRU4Rec while changing only the readout. Do not add recency weighting simultaneously. If measured cost permits, compare gated K=1 and K=4 readouts using identical gate/projection shapes and parameter counts. Here K denotes readout window size; use a separate configuration name such as num_negatives for the loss pool. Further optional controls are a full-history mean and an order-sensitive encoding of the same recent window. The latter adds capacity unless explicitly matched, and should remain an internal jointly trained recurrent module. Latest-item residual and window=1 should be the same implementation, avoiding an accidental architecture difference. No four-way parameter-matched superiority is established by the cited literature. Do not expand these suggestions into an unaffordable factorial search or combine their predictions.

Shortcut and overfitting risks: the new path can learn frequent co-occurrences, favor popular items, suppress useful long-term preferences or over-rank semantic substitutes. Gate values and aggregate HR do not establish useful history dependence. Perturb earlier history while preserving the recent window, and shuffle the recent window while preserving its latest item. The mean branch should be invariant to the latter, whereas the GRU branch need not be; this probe measures the complete model’s order dependence rather than ordering inside the mean. Use the same trained model for these distribution-shift probes and do not treat them as substitutes for retrained controls. Analyze training-only transition support, item frequency, history length and metadata availability where meaningful, reporting counts. Compare common diagnostic margins and score norms; centered feature singular values/effective rank and cosine distributions may supplement, rather than redefine, the supplied embedding-alignment diagnostic. The reported alignment score alone does not justify an anti-collapse penalty or establish recommendation diversity.

Randomness and reproducibility: preserve preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42. Use a dedicated seed-42 stream or deterministic replay for users, windows and negatives across controlled arms. Initialize shared parameters identically, isolate added-module randomness where practical, and disclose remaining dropout differences. Equal update counts do not imply equal GPU time. Record baseline settings, architecture/configuration, initialization, optimizer, scoring transformation, negative construction, epsilon, reducer, software versions, validation cadence, checkpoint rule, tie-breaking and attempted conditions before claiming reproducibility. These details cannot be recovered from the supplied report alone.

Verification: compare vectorized pooling against a differentiable per-row queue in float64 on random masks, internal gaps, repeated items, all-padding rows, singleton histories, K=1 and K>L. Compare input gradients using identical random upstream gradients. Check causality, zero padding gradients, intended window locality and gradcheck with fixed masks. Repeat in production dtypes with declared absolute/relative tolerances, including long-prefix cancellation cases. Check g=0 baseline equivalence, zero padded outputs, empty-history policy and training/export agreement. Verify BPR-max against the direct formula, differentiable negative weights, repeated candidates, extreme scores, K=1 equivalence, score-shift behavior and dense versus chunked losses/gradients. All checks are proposed, not executed.

Runtime and memory: benchmark representative B,L,D, window sizes and padding densities after warmup, excluding compilation and data transfer. Measure forward, backward and combined execution separately using synchronized CUDA events or torch.utils.benchmark. Rebuild graphs and clear gradients consistently. Report repeated timing medians and variability. Synchronize, record baseline allocated memory, reset peak statistics, run forward/backward, synchronize and report both absolute max_memory_allocated and its increase from baseline. Distinguish allocated from reserved memory. These measurements and diagnostics consume the shared budget; prioritize essential correctness and a small number of controlled comparisons.

Protocol: retain single-GPU execution, maximum 200 epochs, exactly 200 batches per epoch and the shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget including diagnostics, debugging and failed runs. Honor the host SASREC_EPOCHS=200 default despite its retained name. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; all artifacts remain beneath the trial directory. Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl and their routing. Follow the supplied checkpoint-selection rule and select only by unchanged host macro validation HR@10 on 200 users per category with 99 unique negative candidates and evaluation seed 42. Record an unspecified tie rule before execution rather than choosing it after results. Retain per-category results and all attempted conditions. A changed hit changes macro HR by 0.00125; repeated selection on these 800 users risks validation overfitting. Inspiration combined scores are supplied historical summaries, not newly verified results. No hidden-test access, extra datasets, pretrained weights, other-trial checkpoints or seed-robustness claims. Final held-out inference remains the host’s separate step.

Diagnostics: keep log2feats(sequence) returning aligned B x L features, item_emb and predict_score(features, items), family-specific sample_batch and every ModelView field. view.model remains the actual trained nn.Module. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The diagnostic loader remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each B x L. Use common diagnostic negatives independent of the optimization pool and valid positions requiring nonzero input, positive and negative IDs. Retain eps=0.5, null metrics for empty valid samples and null item-category breakdowns because those categories are unavailable. Only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps are available; generic metadata examples do not authorize ratings, review text, prices, stores or item categories. Preserve twenty real training-user full-catalog unseen-item recommendation probes, five per category. Track immediate-choice endorsements separately from broad interest, deferred interest, stale-interest objections, functional duplication, compatibility concerns, unestablished tasks and unidentified content. These descriptive judgments do not replace HR@10 or establish causal intent alignment.

Export: mirror the full readout definition, pooling numerics, window size, dimensions, parameters and unchanged scoring transformation in the embedded predictor writer. Save architecture configuration and empty-history policy with the checkpoint. Export exactly one selected joint GRU checkpoint per category with all four routes. The projection and gate are internal jointly trained components, not independently fitted experts. Do not add transition/popularity score tables, average checkpoints or combine models, scores or ranks. Check inference parity on mixed-length, singleton, internally gapped and empty histories before submission.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch
from torch import nn
import torch.nn.functional as F


def recent_valid_mean(input_embeddings, sequence, window=4):
    """Causal mean of the last `window` real inputs, including current.

    input_embeddings: exact B x L x E tensor supplied to corrected GRU.
    Integer IDs/masks are fixed; embeddings remain differentiable.
    Validate numerical accuracy against a queue reference before use.
    """
    if window < 1:
        raise ValueError('window must be positive')
    if input_embeddings.shape[:2] != sequence.shape:
        raise ValueError('Embedding and sequence shapes must agree')
    batch, length, dim = input_embeddings.shape
    if length == 0:
        return input_embeddings
    valid = sequence.ne(0)
    accumulation_dtype = (
        torch.float32 if input_embeddings.dtype in
        (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16) else input_embeddings.dtype
    )
    x = input_embeddings.to(accumulation_dtype)
    x = x.masked_fill(~valid[..., None], 0.0)
    counts = valid.to(torch.int64).cumsum(dim=1)
    prefix = torch.cat([
        x.new_zeros((batch, 1, dim)), x.cumsum(dim=1)
    ], dim=1)
    removed_count = (counts - window).clamp_min(0)
    boundary = torch.searchsorted(
        counts.contiguous(), removed_count.contiguous(), right=False
    ) + 1
    boundary = torch.where(
        removed_count.gt(0), boundary, torch.zeros_like(boundary)
    )
    earlier_sum = prefix.gather(
        1, boundary[..., None].expand(-1, -1, dim)
    )
    denominator = counts.clamp(min=1, max=window).to(x.dtype)
    pooled = (prefix[:, 1:] - earlier_sum) / denominator[..., None]
    pooled = pooled.masked_fill(~valid[..., None], 0.0)
    return pooled.to(input_embeddings.dtype)


class RecentWindowReadout(nn.Module):
    """Internal module; retain the supplied corrected GRU encoder."""
    def __init__(self, item_dim, feature_dim, window=4):
        super().__init__()
        if window < 1:
            raise ValueError('window must be positive')
        self.window = window
        self.project = nn.Linear(item_dim, feature_dim, bias=False)
        self.gate = nn.Linear(feature_dim + item_dim, 1)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.gate.weight)
        nn.init.constant_(self.gate.bias, -4.0)
        # Apply the recorded baseline initialization policy to project.
        # Construct/initialize additions without changing shared tensors.

    def forward(self, gru_features, input_embeddings, sequence,
                fixed_gate=None):
        valid = sequence.ne(0)
        if sequence.shape[1] == 0:
            return gru_features
        if fixed_gate is not None and float(fixed_gate) == 0.0:
            return gru_features.masked_fill(~valid[..., None], 0.0)
        pooled = recent_valid_mean(
            input_embeddings, sequence, self.window
        )
        recent = self.project(pooled)
        gate = (
            torch.sigmoid(self.gate(torch.cat(
                [gru_features, pooled], dim=-1
            ))) if fixed_gate is None else float(fixed_gate)
        )
        features = (1.0 - gate) * gru_features + gate * recent
        return features.masked_fill(~valid[..., None], 0.0)


def bpr_max_position_losses(positive_scores, negative_scores,
                            score_reg=0.0, epsilon=1e-24):
    """Inputs: valid gathered scores [N] and [N,num_negatives].

    Scores already use the declared host activation.
    Returns per-position losses; apply the ORIGINAL host reducer outside.
    Empty output means skip optimization. No division by negative count.
    """
    if (positive_scores.ndim != 1 or negative_scores.ndim != 2
            or negative_scores.shape[0] != positive_scores.shape[0]
            or negative_scores.shape[1] < 1):
        raise ValueError('Expected N positives and N x K negatives, K>=1')
    if score_reg < 0 or epsilon < 0:
        raise ValueError('Penalty and epsilon must be nonnegative')
    p, n = positive_scores, negative_scores
    if p.dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
        p, n = p.float(), n.float()
    log_weights = F.log_softmax(n, dim=-1)
    log_probability = torch.logsumexp(
        log_weights + F.logsigmoid(p[:, None] - n), dim=-1
    )
    if epsilon:
        log_probability = torch.logaddexp(
            log_probability, log_probability.new_tensor(epsilon).log()
        )
    losses = -log_probability
    if score_reg:
        losses = losses + score_reg * (
            log_weights.exp() * n.square()
        ).sum(dim=-1)
    return losses


def final_nonpadding_features(features, sequence):
    """Zero result for empty rows; preserve host empty-history scoring."""
    if sequence.shape[1] == 0:
        return features.new_zeros((sequence.shape[0], features.shape[-1]))
    positions = torch.arange(sequence.shape[1], device=sequence.device)
    last = positions[None, :].expand_as(sequence).masked_fill(
        sequence.eq(0), -1
    ).amax(dim=1)
    output = features[
        torch.arange(sequence.shape[0], device=sequence.device),
        last.clamp_min(0)
    ]
    return output.masked_fill(last.lt(0)[:, None], 0.0)


# Host integration; these steps require the actual corrected baseline:
# 1. Record architecture, sampler, score activation, epsilon, reduction,
#    initialization, optimizer, validation cadence and checkpoint rule.
# 2. Preserve corrected recurrent handling of padding and original states.
# 3. Inside log2feats(sequence): obtain baseline features and the EXACT
#    transformed input embeddings used by the GRU; apply this readout.
# 4. Score gathered valid positives/negatives with the unchanged scorer.
#    Keep candidate IDs, collisions and reduction fixed across readouts.
# 5. Establish BPR-max control separately if the original objective differs.
#    Do not add recency weighting in the readout comparison.
# 6. Compare ungated versus window=4; optionally window=1 versus window=4.
#    Each condition is independently trained and never fused.
# 7. Verify queue/vectorized outputs and gradients, loss formula,
#    causality, padding, empty rows, score transforms and export parity.
# 8. Measure numerical error, synchronized runtime and allocated memory.
# 9. Preserve ModelView and all required diagnostic interfaces/samples.
# 10. Select only by pinned host macro validation HR@10 within budget.
# 11. Mirror complete architecture/configuration in predictor writer.
# 12. Load one selected joint GRU checkpoint for each of four categories.

originality.positive: Tests a focused distinction between latest-item and several-recent-item evidence while preserving an order-sensitive GRU and a controlled objective.
originality.negative: Pooling, gating and hybrid session representations have close precedents in STAMP and NARM; vectorizing the pool is an implementation improvement rather than a new recommendation principle.

future_potential.positive: Controlled results could establish whether explicit recent context warrants adaptive window lengths, order-sensitive local features or elapsed-time-aware pooling.
future_potential.negative: The extension is incremental and may learn co-occurrence shortcuts. It cannot directly identify compatibility, fulfilled needs or immediate intent, and sparse validation limits strong conclusions.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds one projection, one scalar gate and deterministic pooling without new data inputs or independently fitted predictors.
code_difficulty.negative: The earlier score of 3 understated numerical verification, baseline-specific loss/reduction integration, matched randomness, runtime measurement and predictor-writer consistency.

related_work.title: STAMP: Short-Term Attention/Memory Priority Model for Session-based Recommendation
contributions: Combines latest-item information with broader session context.
Uses the session-wide mean and latest embedding to condition attention; transformed context and latest-item representations interact before scoring.
limitations: Its mean covers the full session rather than a fixed recent window.
Provides a close architectural precedent, not evidence that recent-window averaging improves the supplied GRU4Rec.

related_work.title: Neural Attentive Session-based Recommendation
contributions: Combines the final order-sensitive GRU state with attention over preceding recurrent states.
Reports global-only, local-only and hybrid component comparisons supporting investigation of hybrid context.
limitations: Local context means attention over recurrent states, not raw recent-window averaging.
Its component ablations are not parameter-matched comparisons and do not establish gains under the pinned Amazon protocol.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Defines BPR-max as the negative log of a softmax-weighted sigmoid sum.
Introduces a separate softmax-weighted squared-negative-score penalty.
limitations: Objective benefits depend on sampling, scoring and optimization; the paper does not establish gains for this host baseline or recent-window readout.

related_work.title: Official GRU4Rec PyTorch implementation
contributions: Documents shared popularity-tempered replacement sampling, retained duplicate columns and diagonal-only target exclusion.
Provides concrete BPR-max activation, epsilon and configured-batch-size reduction behavior.
limitations: Its session batching and sampling need not match the supplied corrected RecHarness baseline.
Copying these settings during the readout comparison would introduce additional interventions.

related_work.title: Original GRU4Rec implementation and recommended settings
contributions: Provides the original implementation and recommendations including ELU-0.5 or ELU-1 for BPR-max.
limitations: Recommended activation and regularization settings are reference configurations, not validated choices for the current host scoring scale.

related_work.title: Recformer
contributions: Motivates recommendation-specific learning from textual item attributes.
limitations: Pretraining and Transformer architecture differ from a randomly initialized GRU text encoder.
Does not validate the selected recent-window module.

related_work.title: GRU-D
contributions: Provides a recurrent precedent for learned elapsed-time-dependent hidden-state decay.
limitations: Evidence concerns clinical time series; recommendation gains and intent-sensitive forgetting remain hypotheses.
Timestamp decay is a separate intervention from positional window pooling.

related_work.title: Sequential recommendation augmentation component study
contributions: Motivates separating augmentation effects from contrastive-objective effects through controlled comparisons.
limitations: Does not directly establish gains for the supplied GRU4Rec, recent-window readout or pinned Amazon evaluation.

related_work.title: PyTorch cumulative sums, searchsorted, gather and gradient checking
contributions: Documents boundary lookup semantics used with cumulative valid counts.
Together with cumsum and gather documentation, supports the proposed vectorized causal pooling construction; gradcheck supports derivative verification.
limitations: API semantics do not establish numerical equivalence in production dtypes or a speed advantage.
Prefix subtraction requires explicit cancellation and gradient-error checks.

related_work.title: PyTorch benchmarking utilities
contributions: Provides tools for repeated timing measurements with controlled execution.
limitations: Representative forward/backward workloads, warmup and consistent gradient handling remain necessary.
Allocated and reserved CUDA memory require separate interpretation.
